description: Governed DISPOSITION vocabulary for the audience model (schemas/audience-model.schema.json) — the closed lists a segment record's psychological factors must resolve to. Eight families, one id prefix each: inh_ inhibitors · obj_x_ objections (NOT obj_, reserved for objectives) · aln_ aligners/motivators · thr_ identity threats · gap_ belief gaps · mng_ meaning anchors · rat_ rationalization patterns · aff_ affective patterns. This is Band B-sub's vocabulary (ADRA S6.1–S6.6 psykido builders), lifted from prose into governed ids so that (a) a factor can be cited in a planner's reason trace, (b) two segments naming the same inhibitor name it the same way, and (c) nothing psychological enters a record as free text about people. Populations, not persons: every entry describes something a SEGMENT can plausibly hold.

governance.rule: A segment record may only use ids defined here. A new factor requires an entry + version bump — the validator (tools/validate_audience.py) rejects anything else. Entries carry a status: `seed` = placed to make the contract testable, reverse-specified from a reference course, NOT the product of an Audience Agent pass; `specified` = produced or ratified by an Audience Agent deep pass on a real project. A segment record with status approved may not cite a `seed` entry.

families.inh_: inhibitors — what blocks uptake or action (Inhibitor Vaccination, S6.5)
families.aln_: aligners — values/goals content can align with (Motivation Reinforcer, S6.6)
families.thr_: identity threats — where content can read as an attack on who they are (Empathy Tuning, S6.4)
families.gap_: belief gaps — population-level misconceptions / missing models (Meaning Maker, S6.3)
families.mng_: meaning anchors — what makes this matter to them (Meaning Maker, S6.3)
families.rat_: rationalization patterns — how the population explains away the behavior (ADRA rationalization_pattern)
families.aff_: affective patterns — dominant emotional stance toward the subject (Affective Patterns, S6.1)

values.label: Fear of being underpaid
values.definition: Anticipates that transparency will reveal they earn less than peers; avoids engaging to avoid the confirmation.
values.provenance: seed 2026-09-01 — reverse-specified from the paytrans reference course's persuasive content; replace via Audience Agent pass

values.label: Distrust of HR messaging
values.definition: Reads official communication about pay as spin; discounts it before reading.

values.label: Ranges are just legal cover
values.definition: Holds that posted pay ranges exist to satisfy regulation, not to inform employees.

values.label: Fairness for my crew
values.definition: Motivated by equitable treatment of the people they work alongside; responds to fairness framing.

values.label: Predictability of pay
values.definition: Values knowing how pay will move over time; responds to structure and rules being made visible.

values.label: Seniority not valued
values.definition: Reads range-based pay as erasing the standing earned through tenure.

values.label: Midpoint means average pay
values.definition: Believes the range midpoint is what most people earn, rather than the market reference for a fully proficient role.

values.label: Know where I stand
values.definition: The subject matters because it answers 'where am I, and what would move me'.

values.label: Everyone negotiates anyway
values.definition: Explains away range discipline: the range is a fiction because deals get cut regardless.

values.label: Defensive
values.definition: Approaches the subject braced for bad news or blame.

values.label: Indifferent
values.definition: Does not expect the subject to affect them; low arousal.

values.label: Anxious
values.definition: Approaches the subject with worry about consequences or exposure.

values.label: Curious
values.definition: Approaches the subject wanting to understand; open.
